Confirmed: (1) T83's escaped-bracket closure holds for all 21 spellings at all four boundaries; (3) the pre-existing quadratic T83 removed is real, reproduced on the reconstructed pre-change copy; (4) the interrupted attempt's 18-case discovery is real, pre-existing, renderer-fetched and released at all four boundaries, but is TWO distinct classes (a block-container line-anchor gap with no narrow fix, and an escape-blind bracket-depth-pairing gap with a plausible narrow fix), not one. Item (2) is only PARTIALLY confirmed: while re-running the interrupted attempt's own cost probe I found and independently reproduced a THIRD, previously-unreported blocker -- an unmemoized destination-read function that is quadratic on a shape none of the last four rounds' ladders tried, costing 7.4-7.8s at all four public boundaries at under 200KB and ~198s in the detector alone at 1MB, with no attacker host needed at all. All three blockers are confirmed pre-existing (not T83 regressions) and all three fire the scope decision's one exception (blocker reproduced at a public boundary).

findings.problem: readDefinitionDestination (exfil.ts:719-736) reads a reference definition's destination with a sticky regex, REFERENCE_DESTINATION = /\s*(?:<([^<>\n]*)>|(\S+))/y, at a fixed content offset, and unlike its sibling readInlineDestination (:1027-1055, explicitly memoized by descriptionEnd for exactly this reason) it has no memoization. When many surviving line-start `[` candidates in readReferenceDefinitions's loop (:789-855) share the same `]:` offset -- either because the document has one `]:` for many opens, or because the destination read keeps failing so resumeAt never advances -- the sticky regex is re-evaluated from scratch at that same offset once per line-start. When the remainder of the document past that offset is a long whitespace or newline run with no non-whitespace before end of input, evaluating the regex once costs O(remaining), so evaluating it once per line-start over O(n) line-starts costs O(n^2).
findings.impact: A live, zero-click-reachable denial-of-service in the mandatory floor, requiring no attacker host in the payload at all. destFailWhitespaceTail costs 12631.7ms at 262144 bytes and 198325.1ms at 1048576 bytes in the detector alone (exponent ~2.0); destFailNewlineTail is equally quadratic. All four public boundaries have no length gate before invoking detection and each cost 7.4-7.8 seconds at a mere 196610 bytes. Confirmed pre-existing against a reconstructed pre-T83 copy, statistically indistinguishable in cost from the shipped code on this shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Memoize readDefinitionDestination by its afterColon offset, mirroring readInlineDestination's existing memoization by descriptionEnd.

findings.problem: The line-start test inside readReferenceDefinitions (:789-798) recognises a reference-definition line only when, after skipping [ \t]*, the next byte is `[`. CommonMark's block grammar strips a blockquote marker or a list-item marker before parsing the remaining content as an ordinary paragraph, so `> [a]: URL` and `- [a]: URL` are definitions to a renderer -- but this scanner has no model of block-container structure and never recognises them.
findings.impact: Zero-click exfiltration bypass in the mandatory floor. 12 shapes (blockquote plain/escaped/nested, list dash/star/ordered, various definition/use placements, both reference forms) each have marked fetch the attacker host while detectorFindings is 0, mcpState is "none", and all four public boundaries carry the host. A non-empty allowlist does not help. Confirmed pre-existing against a reconstructed pre-T83 copy.
findings.suggested_fix: No narrow fix exists. Faithful closure needs real block-structure parsing -- container boundaries, nesting depth, lazy continuation -- which this scanner is not.

findings.problem: indexContent (:570-601) pairs `[`/`]` with a plain stack that treats every `]` as a real close, with no backslash-escape awareness, unlike readReferenceDefinitions's definition-side scan which T83 made escape-aware. When an image/link DESCRIPTION contains a backslash-escaped `]` that the plain stack treats as the pair's close, descriptionEnds (:627-635) computes both of its candidate ends as the same wrong position, and the correct end is never offered, so the construct is not recognised as an image/link at all.
findings.impact: Zero-click exfiltration bypass for inline and full-reference spellings whose description carries an escaped `]`. Confirmed pre-existing against a reconstructed pre-T83 copy.
findings.suggested_fix: A narrower fix is plausible than F-002's: extend the escape-parity check already implemented twice in this file into indexContent's stack-building loop. Confined to one function and a precedented technique, but needs the disjointness argument re-derived and a differential fuzz re-run against every consumer of descriptionEnds.
